pairs.difference: A: the hay bale sits a little low and is angled 3/4, with the striped wall left open in the top third. Its chunky block reads at once as a bale at thumbnail size. B: the book is tilted diagonally and fills the card (subject area 0.527, above the real 0.233-0.475). The cover stickers, pins and route lines turn into small competing marks at thumbnail size, so the object is slower to name.
pairs.fix: Draw the book about 15% smaller with clear wood showing on all sides. Replace the many cover stickers with one large simple emblem.

pairs.difference: A: the popcorn cart is angled 3/4, with the handle left, the wheel right and a scalloped awning, and runs tall in the card (height 0.869). Its silhouette has a varied edge and names itself at once. B: the barrel stands dead-centre and front-on as an even, symmetrical block, with a wide even gap on all sides (margin 0.142, above the real top of 0.098). It reads as placed in the middle rather than framed.
pairs.fix: Draw the barrel larger, turned slightly to 3/4 and set a little off-centre so it comes closer to the card edges.

pairs.difference: A: the vending machine is a solid blue block turned 3/4, filling the height, and reads as a big mass at thumbnail size. B: the lantern is narrow and dead-centre (width 0.474, area 0.222, both below the real range). Its thin handle and see-through globe carry little mass, wide orange space sits on both sides, and the table band across the bottom takes attention.
pairs.fix: Draw the lantern wider and bigger so it fills most of the card, turned slightly 3/4, with a thicker frame and handle and only a thin hint of table.

pairs.difference: A: the neon ice cream fits whole, top to bottom, inside the card, with height 0.877 above the real top of 0.863, and it hangs slightly tilted against a plain green wall. It reads instantly. B: the viewer is cropped by the bottom edge like the real cropped lighthouse lesson, leans off-axis and sits large in the upper left. The skyline is busy but stays pale behind it. The lessons show generated cards fitting the whole object in the frame and real ones allowing a crop, so A leans generated. The evidence is thin.
pairs.fix: Enlarge the sign slightly and let the bottom tip of the cone run off the card edge. Shift it off-centre.

pairs.difference: A: the stagecoach sits whole and complete, 3/4 in the middle of the desert, with clouds, buttes and pebbles arranged around it, which is the fit-everything-in staging seen in the generated lessons. B: the coaster runs off the bottom and right edges (width 1.0), the car train forms a strong diagonal, and the large foreground car leads the eye. This is the more deliberate crop, though the thin blue track is harder to name at thumbnail size.
pairs.fix: Move in closer on the stagecoach so a wheel or the rear runs off the edge. Drop the distant buttes and pebbles.

pairs.difference: A: the hat is floating and tilted, spans almost edge to edge, and has a low height of 0.512. B: the pair of flip-flops is laid on a diagonal and fills the card like the real fins card. Both sit on plain patterned backgrounds with nothing competing, and both are named instantly at thumbnail size. Composition gives no reason to choose.

A: the guitar is a thin shape pushed to the lower right (area 0.169, below the real 0.237). The bright spotlight cones, truss towers and lamps fill the upper card and fight it at thumbnail size. Only the red body reads first, and the neck fades into the staging. B: the horse is a broad side-on shape spanning the card (width 0.842), with a fence and sky that stay behind it and a clear first read.
pairs.fix: Draw the guitar much larger and fill the card with it, tilted. Remove the spotlight beams and truss towers, leaving a plain soft stage backdrop.

pairs.difference: A: the cactus stands dead-centre, upright and symmetrical, nearly touching the top with its flower (height 0.865 above the real 0.827, width 0.623 below the real 0.661). It is static but instantly named. B: the slide is off-axis, coils across the card (width 0.914) and sits on a cropped pool corner. It is busier but framed with more movement. The centred symmetry of A leans generated.
pairs.fix: Lean the cactus slightly, turn it a touch 3/4 and set it off-centre, with one arm reaching toward the card edge and more space above the flower.

pairs.difference: A: the glass is tall with a diagonal straw and paper umbrella breaking out to the upper corners, so the shape reaches the edges (height 0.89). B: the jug sits dead-centre on a table in concentric pink rings, with a wide even gap around it (margin 0.129, above the real top of 0.108). It is clear but sits smaller and more stiffly in the frame, the same pattern as the barrel in p02.
pairs.fix: Draw the jug larger and closer to the card edges, slightly 3/4 and off-centre, with less table showing.

pairs.difference: A: the neck pillow is one huge tilted blue mass filling the card (area 0.418), though it stands close to the real limit and its margin of 0.112 is just above the real top. B: the wreath is small in the upper-middle of the door (area 0.081, width 0.437, far below the real range). The blue door, frame and ivy cover the card and read first, so the hero loses to its setting.
pairs.fix: Fill the card with the wreath itself, large and centred, with only a plain hint of door behind it. Remove the ivy and frame.

pairs.difference: A: the bandana floats centred with its two knots reaching near the side edges (width 0.912). B: the towel lies on a diagonal, filling the card (area 0.405). Both are single clear shapes on quiet patterned backgrounds with the same breathing room, and both sit within the real occupancy range. Composition gives no reason to choose.

A: the oil lamp stands upright and dead-centre on the rays. It is narrow and small (width 0.426, area 0.17, both below the real range), wide empty green sits on both sides, and the pale glass chimney fades into the light rays. B: the gold pan is tilted, wide (width 0.844) and thrown across the card with its handle to the upper right, like the real tilted cards. The gold nuggets draw the eye inside it.
pairs.fix: Draw the lamp much bigger and wider, with a fuller rounded base, tilted a little and set off-centre, so it fills most of the card.

pattern: Generated cards tend to place the hero whole, upright and dead-centre, with an even gap all around, so the object feels placed rather than framed. Real cards push the hero larger, tilt or turn it 3/4, set it off-axis, and sometimes crop it. Generators also add staging such as spotlights, doors, ivy, rocks and tables, which competes with or shrinks the hero at thumbnail size. Slim objects end up with low occupancy and wide empty sides. Occupancy outside the real range was the strongest measured signal, but most calls here are low confidence, because composition alone separates only the staging and centring extremes.
